feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's attempt to evaluate the limit by direct substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{1}{f(x)} & ={lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{1}{5sin⁡(2x)} \\  & =\frac{1}{5sin⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})} \\  & =\frac{1}{5sin⁡(\pi )} \\  & =\frac{1}{0},\end{aligned}
$$

which is undefined.

Therefore, to find the limit, let's sketch the graph of $y=\frac{1}{5sin⁡(2x)}=\frac{1}{5}csc⁡(2x).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13939267/assets/e3f5c484211ef0b9cf5f3a29198d25c23933a1c07427d0dcbfad01edbb300d0e.png)

From the graph, as $x$ approaches $\frac{\pi }{2}$ from the left, the values of $y=\frac{1}{5}csc⁡(2x)$ are positive and increase without bound. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{1}{f(x)}={lim}_{x\to \,(\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{1}{5}csc⁡(2x)=\infty .
$$
